sources.content: Proposal IV-212: passkey sign-in for Ilvatrice. Motivation: in the last quarter, 31 percent of Ilvatrice support tickets were password resets, and phishing reports rose to 140 cases. This change adds WebAuthn passkeys as a sign-in method next to passwords. A signed-in user can register up to 5 passkeys from the Security page. Registering a passkey requires the user to have entered their password within the last 10 minutes. Passwords stay available; this proposal does not remove them. The owner is the Identity team, and the design review took place on 2026-09-14.

Limits and rollout. Passkeys are stored as public keys in the `credentials` table; the private key never leaves the user's device. Accounts that use single sign-on through an employer are out of scope and keep their current flow. Rollout runs in three stages: 5 percent of web users in week 1, 50 percent in week 3, and all web users in week 5. Mobile apps follow in a later proposal. The feature flag is `auth.passkeys.enabled`. Rollback means turning the flag off; existing passkeys then stop working until it is on again.

claims.text: An Ilvatrice user can register up to 5 passkeys from the Security page.
To register a passkey, an Ilvatrice user must have entered their password within the previous 10 minutes.
The Ilvatrice passkey rollout reaches all web users in week 3.
The Ilvatrice passkey feature flag is named auth.passkeys.enabled.
Accounts that use single sign-on through an employer are out of scope for the Ilvatrice passkey proposal.
Password resets made up 31 percent of Ilvatrice support tickets in the last quarter.
